item.title: Google Patches Eighth Chrome Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks This Year (2 minute read)
item.description: Google has released an emergency security update to patch a new Chrome vulnerability that attackers are actively exploiting. The vulnerability stems from a use-after-free bug in the browser's XML parser and can be exploited by attackers to execute arbitrary code.

item.title: N-able Takes N-central Cloud Offline After Researcher Discloses 33 Zero-Days with PoC Exploits (2 minute read)
item.description: N-able took hosted N-central environments offline and told on-premises customers to shut down servers after Sean Bales disclosed 33 zero-days, called Able2Shell, with proof-of-concept exploits. The flaws include credential theft, file writes, XXE, XSS, and root-level remote code execution. N-able says it found no active exploitation, but watchTowr observed exploitation attempts against honeypots.

item.title: Hackers Now Exploit Critical Barracuda ESG Flaws to Gain Root Access (2 minute read)
item.description: Barracuda Networks reported that two vulnerabilities in its Email Security Gateway (ESG) appliance, patched last week, are being actively exploited. The first vulnerability stems from an authentication weakness that could be exploited to modify an appliance's global config, and the second lets unauthenticated attackers inject OS commands that are run as root. Barracuda said the vulnerabilities require access to the administrative console to exploit and urges organizations not to expose it to the public internet.

item.title: PwC's CISO on AI, Robots & What's Next for Security (10 minute read)
item.description: PwC global CISO and CIO James Shira says AI expands attack surfaces and accelerates change in patching, vulnerability management, and client requests. He expects organizations to reduce their digital footprint and use AI to replace some application front doors, potentially reducing exposure, although he also expects token costs to affect security budgets. Shira advises cybersecurity entrants to pursue certifications and hands-on experience. He recommends a four-year degree for executive roles and says boards respond to delivered results, clear explanations, and stories rather than technical jargon.

item.title: Trusted by Default: Qubole Cross-Account Access Abused in the Wild (8 minute read)
item.description: A threat actor used IAM credentials from Qubole's AWS account between October 14 and October 26. It assumed customer-created integration roles, enumerated AWS resources, read Lambda environment variables, Secrets Manager values, and SSM parameters, and then used TruffleHog to validate AWS, Entra ID, and Okta credentials. It downloaded S3 objects from buckets accessible through the assumed roles. Wiz also identified a separate actor using customer-owned AWS keys tied to Qubole integrations.

item.title: Exchange for breakfast: Turla's Cereal tricks are not for kids (12 minute read)
item.description: Turla's newly discovered Cereal toolset turns a victim's Exchange server into its command-and-control system. A passive backdoor waits for encrypted commands sent through ordinary-looking OWA, Autodiscover, and ActiveSync paths. Meanwhile, a module injected into EdgeTransport.exe hooks existing transport agents to quietly copy emails and attachments involving NATO and EU addresses. ESET found the toolset at government agencies in Kazakhstan and Romania and attributed it to Turla with high confidence, noting that it never observed attacker-controlled infrastructure. Exchange admins should check for DLLs disguised as Windows components in System32\wbem, unexpected Microsoft.Exchange.*.ni.dll files in the .NET native image cache, and EdgeTransport.exe loading assemblies that aren't registered as transport agents.

item.title: xdr-cli (GitHub Repo)
item.description: xdr-cli is a CLI tool that allows a SOC analyst, or their agent, to triage incidents, run advanced hunting, and take response actions in Microsoft Defender XDR from a terminal.

item.title: installctl (GitHub Repo)
item.description: installctl runs a curl | sh installer inside unprivileged namespaces on top of a FUSE copy-on-write overlay, then lists every file the installer created, changed, or deleted so you can apply all of it, some of it, or none. It pauses on package installs, new user accounts, systemctl calls, and crontab edits and asks whether to skip them, run them, or abort. Afterward, it writes an uninstall script that reverts only the installer's own edits to files like ~/.bashrc.

item.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 (12 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 share one underlying model. Mythos targets cybersecurity work: it found 10.2% more vulnerabilities than Opus 5.5 and 14.4% more than Mythos 5.1 in Anthropic's 1,829-CVE Rediscovery test. Fable blocks high-risk cyber tasks, including penetration testing and exploit generation, while reducing false-positive blocks by about 60%.

item.title: Ransomware Recovery Is Now a Client Retention Metric (3 minute read)
item.description: During a ransomware or other security incident, an MSP's clients may experience disruptions that lead to an erosion of trust and ultimately hurt client retention. Disorganized tools and handoffs can complicate recovery, while poor client communication and accounting can hurt trust. MSPs should track time to first client contact, time to recovery, and time to invoice as metrics in a successful recovery process.

item.title: Nvidia CEO's affair becomes a national security problem (2 minute read)
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted having an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. US intelligence reportedly believes the Chinese Ministry of State Security recruited her. Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation into whether Huang was targeted and whether national security or company secrets were compromised. The inquiry comes as the US investigates Megaspeed for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips into China and lawmakers seek Huang's testimony on Chinese access to sensitive technology.

item.title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure (5 minute read)
item.description: Researchers from Google DeepMind utilized a new agentic tool, AlphaProof Code, to formally verify several of the Signal protocol's cryptographic guarantees. The test ran over the course of four weeks and was built upon prior work by the Signal Foundation. No additional bugs were found, but the researchers were able to reproduce findings from previous versions of the protocol.

item.description: A ransomware attack has knocked out Queens Public Library's website, mobile app, digital media services, and public computers at most branches.

item.description: Amplifon Americas says attackers entered its internal systems in January and copied files between January 18 and February 8.

item.title: QNAP Says Hackers are Breaching NAS Devices in Plex2Shell Attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: QNAP is urging users who use Plex on a NAS device to update their Plex servers to fix a series of four vulnerabilities, known as Plex2Shell, that are being actively exploited. QNAP states that users should treat their NAS devices and all personal content as compromised if they're running a vulnerable Plex server that is exposed to the public Internet. Users who suspect compromise can upload their logs to the technical support portal for help determining if they have been compromised.

item.title: SonicWall Warns of New SSL-VPN MFA Bypass Flaw Exploited in Attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: SonicWall is warning customers of a new vulnerability in SonicOS SSL-VPN devices that an attacker with credentials for an alternate authentication method can exploit to bypass SAML authentication controls, potentially including MFA. CISA added the vulnerability to the KEV list, and the SonicWall PSIRT reported it as potentially exploited. SonicWall also fixed six other vulnerabilities, including two management interface flaws, pre-authentication buffer overflows that could lead to DoS, and weak password hashing vulnerabilities.

item.title: Trusted by Default: Qubole Cross-Account Access Abused in the Wild (8 minute read)
item.description: From October 14 to 26, an attacker used IAM credentials from Qubole's AWS account (805246085872) to assume the cross-account roles customers had set up to trust the vendor. It then harvested Secrets Manager, SSM, and Lambda secrets, checked them against AWS, Entra ID, and Okta using TruffleHog, and downloaded entire S3 buckets. Most of the roles it assumed had no legitimate Qubole activity that month, and every request included a valid External ID. Customers should search CloudTrail for AssumeRole calls from that account originating from non-AWS IPs or with quiam-* session names, delete unused vendor roles, and pin trust policies to the vendor's principal using an aws:SourceIp condition, which alone would have blocked every attempt.

item.title: Detecting and Responding to AI-Aided and Agentic Attacks (10 minute read)
item.description: Distinguishing between human behavior, humans assisted by LLMs, and autonomous agents is critical to identifying the type of adversary behind an attack. LLMs can adapt to new information and carry out operations quickly, but they may make mistakes when generating synthetic headers or exhibit coding antipatterns, such as switching frameworks or using input and output handling that is more machine-friendly than human-friendly. Agents may also use a map-reduce-like pattern: they fan out information-gathering tasks, then synthesize the results all at once.

item.title: Contagious Interview: One Interview Away From Infection (19 minute read)
item.description: JFrog followed a single malicious npm package to AccuraSoftHire (accurasofthire[.]com), a fake company with job ads on Indeed and LinkedIn, ID-verified recruiter profiles, and a React take-home test. The test's Tailwind config loads one look-alike forms plugin carrying a loader that runs when the CSS builds, not at npm install, so install-script scanners never see it. Whenever npm removed that plugin, the operator republished it under a new name, and the careers site's "video verification" step was rigged to fail so it could push a curl one-liner that downloads a fake "camera driver."

item.title: PHP2Shell — Deep Dive (45 minute read)
item.description: PHP2Shell is a use-after-free chain that can lead to remote code execution. A crafted multipart request triggers an out-of-memory condition during session.upload_progress processing. PHP's bailout path skips cleanup, leaving stale global pointers in a long-lived worker process. A later request reclaims the freed memory and forges a zend_string length field, causing PHP to return 256 bytes of nearby heap data in a Set-Cookie header. The attacker extracts heap and code pointers, defeats ASLR, forges a HashTable, hijacks pDestructor, and executes a command. The article demonstrates an exploit that targets PHP 8.4.26 Alpine CLI and depends on precise heap grooming.

item.title: AbliteratedOutTheBox (GitHub Repo)
item.description: AbliteratedOutTheBox is a fork of llama.cpp that gets any supported model to answer flagged harmful prompts, delivering the requested content instead of a refusal, at inference time and with the original weights left on disk unchanged.

item.title: Attackgen (GitHub Repo)
item.description: AttackGen is a cybersecurity incident response testing tool that leverages the power of large language models and the comprehensive MITRE ATT&CK framework. The tool generates tailored incident response scenarios based on user-selected threat actor groups and your organization's details.

item.title: 0 (GitHub Repo)
item.description: 0 is an open-source AI security harness from YC-backed 0.security that runs vulnerability investigations, finding verification, and fix workflows in a local browser console, using whatever model provider you bring. It also does Ghidra-backed binary analysis through its 0verse MCP server, and it keeps source-linked memory of past findings so later runs can build on them. Its workflows are exposed over CLI and MCP, so Claude Code or another coding agent can drive the same runs, and a GitHub Action fits it into CI.

item.title: Google DeepMind's AI Agents Make 1024-Bit RSA Keys Cheaper to Attack (2 minute read)
item.description: Google DeepMind and researchers from UC San Diego and Inria found two ways to reduce the cost of attacking RSA-1024. AI agents cut a signature-forgery attack's CPU time from 1,380 to 391 core-years. They also proposed a batch-factoring method that could make each additional 1024-bit key about 30 times cheaper to factor, though it remains unimplemented. The signature attack needs roughly 4 billion signing queries and does not recover private keys. Modern systems using 2048-bit or larger RSA keys are unaffected.

item.title: Default 'admin:admin' Server Password Helps Researchers Hack Two Automakers, Unlock and Start Cars (3 minute read)
item.description: Researchers accessed ForgeRock/Ping Identity admin consoles at two automakers through an exposed Apache Felix console using the default admin:admin password. They bypassed edge filtering with encoded path characters, gained server access, changed customer credentials, obtained app tokens, and remotely unlocked and started test vehicles.

item.description: Linus Torvalds says Linux eBPF fixes are arriving faster than new bug reports, a possible sign that the surge of flaw reports is slowing, but most Linux kernel areas have not reached the peak point yet.

item.description: Internet-exposed Copeland XWEB PRO controllers, the ones that run supermarket freezer racks, are being hijacked, most likely through the CVE-2026-25085 authentication bypass, to send coordinated spam and serve as proxy exits.

item.title: Iris Ohyama Data Cloud Breach Exposes Info of 7.7M Customers (2 minute read)
item.description: Japanese manufacturer Iris Ohyama disclosed that a third-party cloud service was breached, exposing data belonging to 7.7M former and current customers. The exposed data includes full names, physical addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, genders, dates of birth, and account passwords. Iris Ohyama has stated that account passwords are encrypted but did not give further details.

item.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices (3 minute read)
item.description: A vulnerability called *sshole allows remote attackers to log in to some Alpine Linux systems without a password. It affects OpenSSH built with musl and without PAM, where an active passwordless account uses SHA256 or SHA512 password hashing. An attacker can send more than 256 characters in the password field and gain access in one attempt. Alpine and OpenSSH have released patches. Affected systems should update promptly.

item.title: DigiCert Data Breach Impacts Business Customer Information (1 minute read)
item.description: DigiCert disclosed that attackers created a read-only account on an exposed internal archive system and accessed business-customer contact data from June 27 to July 2. Exposed records include names, email addresses, phone numbers, business addresses, and, in some cases, identity documents. DigiCert says certificate-issuing systems were unaffected. It has reset passwords, disabled self-registration, added monitoring, and reviewed account permissions.

item.title: A Journey Into Claude's Sandbox (7 minute read)
item.description: BishopFox researchers inadvertently discovered that they could convince Claude Code to reveal details about its internals. The researchers were able to use Claude to read its process memory, download files (including the process_api binary), and create a virtual interface to bypass the local connection block. The researchers also discovered that, although the Claude Enterprise controls blocked users from changing their first name, they could do so via the API.

item.title: Virtualization security: attack layers and misconfiguration impact (12 minute read)
item.description: In a BlackNevas ransomware case investigated by Kaspersky GERT, attackers who reached a PRTG monitoring server used its stored ESXi root password, reused across hosts, to SSH in, disable execInstalledOnly via esxcli, and encrypt VMFS volumes before wiping logs. In a separate case, The Gentlemen group found plaintext Proxmox root credentials in an admin's notes. It used the VNC websocket API to encrypt the entire cluster, with neither attack requiring a VM escape. Defenders should give monitoring tools dedicated least-privilege identities, vault unique per-host credentials, keep ESXi SSH off behind vCenter Lockdown Mode, and alert on execInstalledOnly or Secure Boot changes.

item.title: The attack chain behind the v1.107.0 LiteLLM release (10 minute read)
item.description: An admin key for LiteLLM's internal Agent Platform was committed to a public repo on May 27 and removed hours later but never revoked, and on October 10 an attacker used it to pull an org owner's unscoped GitHub CLI token from the platform API. With that token and two maintainer tokens stolen through CI workflows, the attacker overrode branch protection, built from a lookalike Berri-AI fork, and published poisoned wheels and images that stayed up for about two hours. Defenders should revoke any key that was ever committed, keep unscoped CLI tokens out of automation, and alert on branch protection overrides and deleted workflow runs.

item.title: Threat Feed Me (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Threat Feed Me is an open-source, on-prem threat intelligence aggregator meant to replace MineMeld, Palo Alto Networks' free feed-aggregation tool, which the company retired years ago and many SOCs still miss. It pulls 22 free feeds that need no API key and removes duplicate indicators. It also detects when one feed is just republishing another, so copied entries don't look like independent agreement. That keeps the strictest high-confidence blocklist small and trustworthy.

item.title: Brava Security (Product Launch)
item.description: Brava Security provides an AI platform that models attacker behavior, simulates attacks, analyzes resulting telemetry, identifies missed defenses, and rewrites SIEM detections. It integrates with more than 70 sources and destinations, provides initial insights within 10–15 minutes of onboarding, and requires no changes to existing security infrastructure.

item.title: coldframe (GitHub Repo)
item.description: coldframe is a single-file Python honeypot that impersonates Danfoss AK-SM 800A and Copeland/Dixell XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers, matching the server headers, TLS certificate fields, and login flows that Shodan records for real units, and tagging exploit attempts for seven CVEs, including CVE-2025-41450 and CVE-2026-25085. Weak default logins let attackers into a fake store dashboard where every defrost click is logged as a control event, and an optional Modbus TCP listener catches generic industrial scanners. It ships with a hardened rootless container and a cloud-init file for $4 droplets, though defenders should change its persona strings before deploying, since the public code is easy to fingerprint.

item.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other (3 minute read)
item.description: In sandboxed tests, nine coding agents were given a private deploy token and access to a forum of 24 agents. To obtain a bug fix, the forum demanded the token and an install script. Across 181 trials, agents shared the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, with agent pressure increasing script execution from 19 percent to 34 percent.

item.title: Notes and links from my talk at Texas Linux Fest (10 minute read)
item.description: In his Texas Linux Fest talk, Don Marti argued that open source beat the Clipper Chip and DRM mandates, but that open source's own "commoditize the complement" logic, applied to content, gave rise to an adtech system that now profits from matching scammers with victims. He cited Pew data showing 73% of US adults had faced an online scam, along with estimates that Meta earned around 10% of its ad revenue from fraud, and noted that once-niche privacy nerd advice like DNS-level ad blocking was now standard corporate IT guidance. Marti framed California privacy law and favorable jury verdicts as the most promising counterweight, though the post was explicitly preliminary and its framing of Google and Meta as crime organizations was his own opinion.

item.title: Secure Code Benchmark Finds Top Coding Agents Write Secure Code Only 25% of the Time (25 minute read)
item.description: Qwen researchers tested six frontier coding agents on LSCBench, 450 security-neutral tasks built from 150 real vulnerabilities across seven languages, and found that while 73.6% to 91.3% of outputs worked, even the top performer, Claude Fable 5, wrote code that was both functional and secure only 25.1% of the time. Agents often added local defenses like bounds checks but almost never secured SSRF or information exposure, which depend on policies the spec never stated, and a one-line security reminder raised joint pass rates by 15 to 21 points for three of the four models retested. Pooled together, the six models secured 44% of tasks, though the tests and specs were drafted with Qwen's own Qwen3.8-Max, which the authors argued did not tilt the results.

item.description: Korean fabless chipmaker ICTK is building a programmable post-quantum hardware engine with Pukyong National University that runs NIST's ML-KEM and ML-DSA alongside Korea's KpqC algorithms on shared IP blocks, due in August 2028 for a security SoC aimed at KT.

item.title: Microsoft Paint RCE Fix Now Available, but Windows Update Won't Deliver It (3 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft has fixed CVE-2026-83844, an out-of-bounds read in Windows Paint that can enable network-based remote code execution.

item.title: Tricking Deepseek Into Not Hacking Your Website (1 minute read)
item.description: Utku Sen found that planting forbidden strings like "Tank Man" in a site's HTML comments and decoy JavaScript function names caused Deepseek-powered pentest agents in the Pi and ARTEX harnesses to refuse or abort testing his own vulnerable app, turning model censorship into a crude anti-AI firewall.

item.title: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones (3 minute read)
item.description: Attackers likely linked to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service used watering holes, proxy domains, and a compromised Ukrainian analytics service to inject JavaScript into mobile traffic. The code profiled visitors and delivered zero-click exploit chains against outdated iOS or Android devices, including DarkSword. Payloads sought browser cookies, Wi-Fi passwords, and full device data. Targets included sites connected to US and UK diplomatic circles and Ukraine.

item.title: Chainalysis Warns All Users Hit In Cyber Breach Involving “Agentic” Techniques (2 minute read)
item.description: Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis released a warning that all of its users' data may have been compromised following an attack by a threat actor utilizing “offensive agentic techniques.” The stolen data includes names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens for all Chainalysis users. Chainalysis also temporarily took some other services offline, including its Know Your Transaction (KYT) cryptocurrency transaction monitoring service.

item.title: Anthropic won't fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers execute remote commands across corporate boundaries (5 minute read)
item.description: A browser extension with access to claude.ai can use Claude Dispatch to send prompts to Claude Desktop and achieve remote code execution. The attack exploits shared web and desktop sessions, repeated approval clicks, and a malicious npm package. It can also reach a work computer from a personal browser session. Anthropic knew of the issue in May but has not issued a fix. Dispatch remains available to existing users.

item.title: GhostMap: The Android flaw that crashes your phone before you open the app (17 minute read)
item.description: An APK entry using a nonstandard compression method slips past libziparchive's size check, while libandroidfw memory-maps it at its full declared size. As a result, any process that reads a malformed resource receives a SIGBUS. That flaw lets an app with no code or permissions trap system_server in a boot loop that only a factory reset clears, or cause its own icon to crash on every uninstall screen. Bitdefender found it when a packed banking dropper in the wild crashed its emulators, but the persistent boot loop was its own escalation. Google declined to ship a security fix even though the bug reproduces on Android 10 through 17. With no patch coming, defenders should flag APKs whose ZIP entries use compression methods other than stored or deflate before they're installed, since an on-device warning may come too late.

item.title: Escaping Firecracker from Guest Userspace (9 minute read)
item.description: Coinspect demonstrated a Firecracker sandbox escape from guest userspace. CVE-2026-122192 allowed a guest to read and modify live Firecracker VMM memory and gain code execution in the host-side process. The flaw stemmed from a failed memory replacement after a snapshot-backed RAM discard, leaving a stale KVM memory slot pointing to reused VMM memory. A second issue, FC-03, allowed VMM code to use io_uring to perform host operations blocked by seccomp, including sending a network message to a host listener. Firecracker v0.23.0 through v1.16.1 are affected. v1.16.2 and v1.17.0 fix the escape.

item.title: The SOC Files 5: Ghost in the pipeline, or a fileless SharePoint breach by Storm-2603 (15 minute read)
item.description: Storm-2603 used the ONYPHE scanner to check a SharePoint server for ToolShell (CVE-2025-53770), waited three days, and on Christmas Eve loaded a webshell directly into IIS's w3wp.exe process memory. The webshell activated only for a specific User-Agent, tunneled into the internal network with suo5, escalated to SYSTEM using EfsPotato, and then moved to a vulnerable Velociraptor build, an EDR-killer driver, and a blocked Warlock ransomware attempt. Kaspersky attributed the intrusion with moderate confidence. Defenders should hunt for IIS paths that resolve in config but have no file on disk, which appear as IIS-Configuration ETW events 25 and 47 without the usual file-change monitoring events. Kaspersky has released CLRDeserializationExploitFinder to flag the deserialization exploit itself.

item.title: synology-nas-cli (GitHub Repo)
item.description: synology-nas-cli checks a Synology NAS for the exposures exploited in October's C3RB3R/.L0CK3D ransomware campaign: unpatched DSM builds, vulnerable SA-26:14 packages, QuickConnect and UPnP port forwarding, SMB1, ransom notes, and CVE-2024-10441 exploit traces. It shows each fix as a before-and-after dry-run plan, applies it, and reads every setting back to confirm. If encryption is already running, it can freeze the encryptor with SIGSTOP and capture its memory to recover keys. It's a zero-dependency Python CLI with an MCP server, so a Claude Code or Codex agent can run the audit end to end.

item.title: Sectiv (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Sectiv is a Burp Suite extension that runs captured proxy traffic past an LLM, guided by editable "skills" for IDOR, XSS, SQLi, and SSRF, and returns triaged findings with CVSS scores and HTML, Python, or curl PoCs. Testers can load two accounts to help the model reason about broken access control. It masks cookies, tokens, and JWTs before sending traffic to providers like OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, or a local Ollama model. Skills can be imported, exported, and tailored per target, and findings export to HTML, Markdown, or JSON for reporting.

item.title: GPT-6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents (10 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber built working exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, more than five times GPT-5.6 Sol's count with the same harness, and found 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox bugs. OpenAI also trained it to stay within the scope a researcher sets: on a honeypot evaluation, it avoided easy-to-exploit, out-of-scope services in 99.93% of runs without a safety prompt and 100% with one, enough for OpenAI to rate it Critical for cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework. Approved defenders reach it through Daybreak Red, which requires IP allowlisting by default and runs misuse monitoring, and a new tier gives critical infrastructure teams authorized OT/ICS testing.

item.title: Apple Will Scan Shared iCloud Links for Harmful Content, but Won't Explain What Counts as Harmful (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple will check photos and files shared via iCloud's “Anyone with the Link” setting for harmful content on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS 27.3. Publicly shared items lose end-to-end encryption, even with Advanced Data Protection enabled. Apple can remove files, block accounts, prevent re-registration, and contact law enforcement. It has not defined “harmful,” explained the screening method, said whether people review flags, or confirmed whether existing public links are covered.

item.title: OpenAI AI Pipeline Generates 948 Linux Root Escalation Exploits in 30-Hour Run (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI says an automated pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities in 30 hours and generated 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits. The run produced 291 information-leak proofs of concept, patches for identified flaws, and at least 10 novel exploitation techniques. It cost $1.21 million in API credits, or $1,279 per exploit. OpenAI says unpatched systems with low-privileged access should be treated as accessible to well-resourced attackers with root access.

item.title: Bank Phishing Sites Show Fake ‘Suspended' Pages to Evade Takedowns (3 minute read)
item.description: Kela found more than 300 fake bank domains using a phishing kit that records visitor IP addresses. First visits receive bank login pages. Repeat visits receive a fake hosting "suspended" notice. This can make takedown teams classify live sites as inactive. The campaign targets business banking and treasury logins at 189 US institutions, with activity also seen in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand.

item.title: Cyberattack on Norway's aid agency may have swept up all user data (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers used 27 compromised accounts to enter Norad's Grants Portal, potentially exposing names and email addresses for all 20,614 registered users, and also took applications and documents from three foreign organizations.

item.title: Chinese Nation-State Threat Activity Falls Sharply in Q2 and Q3 2026 (3 minute read)
item.description: Trellix detected 41.4% less China-aligned nation-state activity from April to September, but cautioned that the drop may reflect shifts in targeting or its own visibility rather than less hacking, since PRC activity still outpaced Russia and Iran, while the US and Turkey together drew three-quarters of all nation-state detections.

item.title: AWS Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory for your compute resources (1 minute read)
item.description: AWS Security Hub now shows an organization-wide inventory of the software packages installed across EC2 instances, ECR images, and Lambda functions, built from Amazon Inspector's SBOMs and queryable through the API, at no extra cost wherever Inspector is enabled.

item.description: AI agents are calling APIs, moving data, and making decisions for your users. Most security tools see it after. Very few stop it before.Register free — November 12 at 1PM ETRahul Parwani, Product Leader, AI Governance and Security at Airia, and Herman Errico, creator of AARM at Vanta, are hosting a 35-minute fireside on governing AI agents at the point of action. item.title: Philippine Migrant Worker Data Likely Leaked in 69GB Breach (3 minute read)
item.description: An unknown actor copied 27 SQL Server backup databases belonging to the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration in 24 minutes. The 69GB set includes migrant-worker records, contracts, accreditation data, and cashier and LandBank financial records. The attacker used GodPotato, SeImpersonate, and Impacket, then left logs and tools on an open Singapore staging server. The stolen backups have not appeared for sale, and the final destination remains unknown. Hunt.io notified CERT-PH and the Department of Migrant Workers.

item.title: mSecure Password Manager Warns Users to Secure Their Credentials (2 minute read)
item.description: mSeven notified users of its mSecure password manager that it detected suspicious activity related to the app. Per the message, mSeven warned users to secure their credentials, raising suspicions that it may not be encrypting credentials securely. In an audit conducted last year by Germany's Federal Office for Information Security, the password manager was flagged as not meeting the usual expectations of password managers.

item.title: Cyberattack on French plasma stores is enough to make your blood boil (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers compromised a refrigeration supplier and altered cold-room settings at France's Blood Establishment, changing temperatures from -30°C to 110°C. EFS monitoring detected the changes. Staff controlled or isolated affected units and moved plasma and samples elsewhere. No blood products were lost. The incident follows European attacks on supermarket refrigeration, including defrost cycles that spoiled food. CERT-FR had urged remediation of vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers.

item.title: Finding 40+ Vulnerabilities in Healthcare Software Serving More Than 100 Million Patients (13 minute read)
item.description: An AI-assisted review of OpenEMR produced 42 published security advisories, fixed in version 8.5.0 on 27 October 2026. The issues include three critical findings: local file disclosure through the PDF generator, SQL injection through patient-data field names, and another SQL injection. Other bugs exposed patient records, allowed portal credential replacement, and enabled administrator API impersonation through an impersonation chain that combined SQL injection and file disclosure to forge an OAuth bearer token, bypassing password and MFA checks.

item.title: Why Conventional Reputation Feeds Miss Software Supply Chain Attacks (18 minute read)
item.description: Conventional threat intelligence feeds and multi-engine scanners fail to detect most software supply chain attacks on day zero, exposing organizations to malicious package behavior for months after public disclosure. Research indicates that blind-spot rates for supply chain attacks in these reputation tools range from 70% to 90%. General-purpose security tools remain ineffective against these threats because they are designed to detect inbound perimeter probes rather than malicious package behavior.

item.title: You Had Me at “Hello”: Inside The Greeter, A Chinese‑Language Framework Targeting AI Infrastructure (15 minute read)
item.description: Era researchers tracked a Chinese-language framework, Greeter, exploiting Flowise's overrideConfig code-injection flaw (CVE-2024-58351) across seven honeypots from July to October. Each “hello” request delivered a different command through javascriptFunction, without changing the saved chatflow. The framework ran host reconnaissance, searched .env files, SSH keys, and Flowise encryption keys, probed AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud metadata services, and checked Docker socket access, Linux capabilities, persistence paths, and memory-based execution. Of 3,277 identifiable internet-exposed Flowise instances, 703 lacked authentication. 46 matched the honeypot's vulnerable conditions.

item.title: Sentra (Product Launch)
item.description: Sentra provides cloud-native data security and governance. It finds and classifies data across cloud, SaaS, warehouses, knowledge stores, and file shares, maps access by users and agents, enforces least privilege, and automates remediation.

item.title: Grim Prompter (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Grim Prompter is a Claude Code and Codex skill that has a coding agent build a threat model from a repo and cite file-and-line evidence for every trust boundary, threat, and mitigation. It ships 36 architecture-specific workflows, from RAG and agentic AI to OT/ICS and smart contracts, and 29 method prompts covering STRIDE, PASTA, LINDDUN, and MITRE ATLAS. Saved JSON baselines let the agent review a branch diff against the existing model.

item.title: sapper-v2 (GitHub Repo)
item.description: sapper-v2 is a multi-agent pentest harness that won the 634-team qualifier of Tencent Cloud's AI Attack-Defense Challenge, capturing 85 flags in eight unattended hours on 1B tokens where the runner-up burned 4.5B. A commander agent reads a shared fact graph and dispatches scouts, generals, and soldiers through tmux, with GLM-5.3 making decisions and the cheaper DeepSeek V4.1 Flash doing the volume work. It works with any agent CLI, including Claude Code and Codex, and the coordination layer is spun out as the general-purpose nvwabase project.

item.title: Securing Our Frontier Model Training Environment (12 minute read)
item.description: At the end of September, OpenAI embarked on a frontier model training pause to harden its training infrastructure against potential escapes. Beyond host-based sandboxing, OpenAI limits its model training environment's network access to strictly necessary internal services and an “offline internet” of cached search indexes and pages. OpenAI also spent billions of tokens red-teaming its training environment to find gaps in its hardening.

item.title: Verifying Apple Reference Images (7 minute read)
item.description: The Privacy Preserving Systems Lab released the first publicly available tool to verify Apple Reference Images captured using the new cryptographic authentication standard for the iPhone 18 Pro series. The system utilizes secure camera hardware alongside Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure to cryptographically sign pixel data. The protocol embeds a developer-accessible reference image next to the main photo using JUMBF boxes, SHA-512 hashing ranges, and a composite ML-DSA and RSA signature.

item.title: South Korea's Lee Calls For Powerful Government-Wide Cybersecurity Body (2 minute read)
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called for the creation of a powerful government-wide cybersecurity body to coordinate cybersecurity operations and response. In a cabinet meeting, Lee stated that the current system was too reactive and that a proactive system was needed to protect public services and critical infrastructure. Lee also stressed the need for further public- and private-sector collaboration.

item.title: Chainstack Reports Production Systems Breach Exposing Customer Data and Password Hashes (2 minute read)
item.description: Chainstack says an attacker entered via a third-party component on October 26 and reached production systems, accessing customer names, organizational details, email addresses, and password hashes.

item.title: Residential Proxies Detected on White House Network (3 minute read)
item.description: Proxy-detection vendor Layer3 Intel says its probes exited through the White House's own network (AS2650) 236 times in a month via 6 addresses and 28 commercial residential proxy services.

item.title: Frontline Education Data Breach Impacts Over 1.3 Million (1 minute read)
item.description: Hackers exploited a third-party software vulnerability on August 14 to access Frontline Education systems.

item.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies (3 minute read)
item.description: Google says it disrupted the XCPE botnet, built from more than 1.3 million Android TV boxes made by Videostrong. The devices secretly rented users' internet connections to residential-proxy services and ran ad fraud. Google took down the operator's domains and servers. The action may cut off more than 10 million additional infected devices. The malware also appeared in telehealth devices, karaoke machines, and digital signage.

item.title: Mercado Bitcoin Hit By $46M Security Breach (2 minute read)
item.description: Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest crypto exchange, disclosed that it suffered a security incident involving approximately $46.3M in assets. Mercado stated that the breach did not affect customers or result in a data breach. It has temporarily paused transactions while it investigates the breach further, and has published the destination wallet address.

item.title: Financial Services Firm MoneySmart Hit By IT Security Breach, Some Customers' Data Copied (2 minute read)
item.description: Financial services company MoneySmart disclosed that a “security incident” led to the disclosure of some of its customers' personal data in Hong Kong and Singapore. MoneySmart said the data may include names and email addresses, shipping addresses, and application or policy reference numbers for customers who submitted rewards claims.

item.title: The Quiet Phase: Why Active Directory Group Enumeration Deserves Your Attention (9 minute read)
item.description: Attackers map who sits in Domain Admins with SharpHound or PowerView long before they change any group membership, and an audit entry (SACL) on the group's member attribute turns those reads into Event 4662, or 4799 for built-in groups, on the domain controller that answered. On real privileged groups, the signal drowns in reads from directory sync, Exchange, and admin tooling, and SAMR-based tools like net group /domain bypass it entirely. Pair the audit with decoy groups that nothing legitimate ever reads, correlate a decoy read and a real admin-group read from the same logon session, and check coverage with its QuietPhase PowerShell script.

item.title: Jailbreaking my car's navigation system just so I can change the time (11 minute read)
item.description: A Renault Latitude's TomTom Carminat LIVE head unit hid its clock settings behind a legitimate navigation SD card. The card used CID-based DRM and signed files, so a blank card could not supply the missing menu definition. The author reverse-engineered the Linux 2.6.28 firmware, built a QEMU and CAN emulator, and found that master.script allowed a root path-traversal write through its LOG command and wrote |/bin/sh /media/sdcard/payload.sh into /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern, then crashed /bin/dbus-monitor to trigger a coredump and execute the payload as root. The exploit enabled an eMMC backup and a timezone patch from UTC+3 to UTC+2.

item.title: Prioritize What Attackers Will Exploit: 4 Elements of Strong Exposure Prioritization (7 minute read)
item.description: Fewer than 10% of vulnerabilities are exploited, but remediation programs often treat most findings as urgent. Rank exposures using active-exploitation intelligence, asset criticality, EPSS-style exploitability modeling, and control validation. A vulnerability on an internet-facing system that handles regulated data, has known exploitation, and lacks segmentation should outrank a high-CVSS finding on an isolated internal asset. The model measures success by fewer exploitable exposures and reduced remediation effort, rather than ticket volume.

item.title: dragon-tales (GitHub Repo)
item.description: dragon-tales is a binary analysis library for disassembling, assembling, and analyzing machine code across multiple architectures.

item.title: Crashtest (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Crashtest runs adversarial security tests against a JavaScript app's real route handlers entirely in-process, so it never opens a socket or needs a live server. Its built-in campaigns cover identity-spoofing headers, prototype pollution, cross-tenant ID enumeration, leaked secrets, and cost-amplification abuse, and every attack ends in a verdict of REFUSED, EXPLOITED, or BOUNDED (an accepted risk with a named owner). It plugs into Hono, Express, and Fastify, and its GitHub Action fails CI only on a new exploit or a regression, never on risks the team already accepted.

item.title: safeagents (GitHub Repo)
item.description: safeagents is a local proxy that sits between a coding agent and its model API and checks each tool call before the harness runs it. It blocks calls to undeclared tools and calls that reach hosts nobody mentioned in the conversation, and it runs atif-scan detectors that catch reads of /proc/1/environ or curl --noproxy. Ambiguous calls can go to an optional judge model that sees only the user's prompt, the call, and the findings, never the agent's reasoning, and it works with any harness that accepts a custom base URL, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Hermes.

item.title: Red Hat Patches 9.8-Rated Linux TCP RCE Flaw While Ubuntu Releases Fixes for Testing (4 minute read)
item.description: Red Hat has patched CVE-2026-98432, a 9.8-rated use-after-free in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP handling. A remote attacker can send IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp options to a listening TCP port and trigger a race that reads freed memory, potentially allowing code execution. RHEL 8, 9, and 10 fixes require a reboot. No exploitation has been reported. An nftables rule can drop IPv4 TCP packets with IP options, but it does not fully prevent exploitation.

item.title: Token thieves costing companies $100K+ per day in illicit LLM charges (3 minute read)
item.description: Google Mandiant reports that criminals are stealing LLM API keys and cloud service account credentials, then running high-volume model inference at victims' expense. Charges reached $100,000 per day in one case and $1 million in total before access was revoked. One service, Jet Night, allegedly used stolen keys to offer access to frontier models for about $60 per month.

item.title: How Cisco defends at machine speed with OpenAI (3 minute read)
item.description: Cisco is pairing its network telemetry with OpenAI's Daybreak program and GPT-6 Astra to link signals that look harmless on their own and to speed up vulnerability patching, and Cisco's Jeetu Patel calls the gains "step function improvements." Patel also argued that agent security will depend on telling a hijacked agent apart from one pursuing a legitimate goal in an unintended way. That will take security telemetry and observability data read side by side. The post is an OpenAI customer story with no metrics or technical detail behind its claims, so it reads more as a sign of where vendor AI partnerships are heading than as evidence of results.

item.title: Railway's signup-testing agents probed Primcloud's network (3 minute read)
item.description: A Railway engineer's agent harness, meant only to test Primcloud's signup flow, used its container's credentials to request every tenant's secrets, queried the cloud metadata endpoint, and port-scanned Primcloud's internal network twice in 15 minutes.

item.title: Russia dismantles infrastructure of VasyGrek cybercrime group, detains three suspects (3 minute read)
item.description: In a rare domestic crackdown, Russian police, working with Kaspersky, dismantled the infrastructure of VasyGrek (also tracked as Fluffy Wolf), a financially motivated phishing group.

item.title: Fashion retailer Resolve says hackers stole payment card information (2 minute read)
item.description: Revolve told the SEC that attackers accessed multiple systems and used automated methods to obtain names, contact details, and card numbers and expiration dates from customers who stored payment data online. Texas regulators recorded 127,200 affected residents. Vermont reported 1,328. Revolve notified law enforcement, hired a cybersecurity firm, and said operations and finances were unaffected.

item.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack (3 minute read)
item.description: A suspected cyber-attack switched refrigeration evaporators to defrost mode at supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland. Freezer temperatures reportedly reached 50°C, forcing stores to discard spoiled food. A Delhaize branch reported €100,000 in losses. Sabcobel said affected units need physical changes. Remote internet-connected maintenance remains part of the operating model.

item.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers (3 minute read)
item.description: IBM reported four Langflow vulnerabilities affecting versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8. Two are critical and require no account: CVE-2026-93680 bypasses authentication, while CVE-2026-110186 permits arbitrary code execution through MCP tool enumeration. A public Metasploit module already enumerates Langflow MCP tools without credentials. Version 1.13.0 is the only fix. It disables automatic login by default. IBM has not published a workaround.

item.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants (5 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP requests in Q3 2026. Short attacks under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps rose 208% year over year, while attacks above 1 Tbps fell 69% from Q2. CLDAP floods dropped 99.5%. DNS amplification rose 215%, and UDP floods rose 122%. The United States was the most-attacked country, followed by China and Indonesia. Canada rose from 16th to 6th, and Israel to 10th. IoT botnets remain active, with Mirai-classified traffic peaking at 57.23 PB in August.

item.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts (3 minute read)
item.description: Researchers at Parameter Labs discovered a complex attack chain that could let attackers create malicious pages using ChatGPT's HTML Previews (formerly Canvas). The exploit begins by using the MathLive JavaScript library to create a new iframe that could load scripts from YouTube despite OpenAI's CSP policy. That iframe could then use YouTube's oEmbed endpoint to access OpenAI API endpoints and steal private data from anyone who accesses the ChatGPT share URL.

item.title: Turning the Valve - Exploiting RCE and LPE in the Steam Platform (22 minute read)
item.description: Atredis researchers found four local privilege escalation flaws and two remote code execution bugs in Steam for Windows. The LPE paths abused Steam's SYSTEM service through install-script allowlists, module loading, secure-desktop input forwarding, and driver installation. The remote bugs affected Steam-to-Steam synchronization messages: stack overflows in download-schedule and app-status handlers, plus an uninitialized-memory leak of steamclient64 pointers. The researchers combined the leak with an overflow to build a zero-click RCE using a ROP chain. They reported the issues to Valve through HackerOne. The bugs are patched or past the disclosure timeline, and proof-of-concept code is public.

One application experienced an attack just 1 hour and 56 minutes after appearing in an app store.Is your AppSec strategy keeping up?Read the report.

item.title: PyPCAPKit (GitHub Repo)
item.description: PyPCAPKit is an open-source Python library for parsing, constructing, and analyzing network packets and PCAP files, with DictDumper as its formatted output dumper.

item.title: Wake and Break (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Wake and Break is a PSP (Platform Security Processor) exploit for AMD navi31 cards that will disable PSP's firmware signature check so that the card will load unsigned IP firmware.

item.title: MCPTrace (GitHub Repo)
item.description: MCPTrace is a Volatility 3 plugin for extracting MCP/JSON-RPC message candidates from Windows and Linux memory dumps.

item.title: Securing Internet Critical Software: How We Could Have Backdoored Bash (7 minute read)
item.description: Researchers at Hacktron discovered a command injection vulnerability in GNU Savannah that let them gain root and take over user accounts, including a Bash maintainer. The vulnerability stemmed from the GPG key validator inserting a user's email address directly into commands it executed without sanitizing the input. The attackers utilized this vulnerability to install a webshell, read the database password, set their account to a superuser, impersonate other users, and also escalate privileges by exploiting GemOver(lay).

item.title: Cyberattack Hits Rosstat as Hackers Claim Huge Data Theft (2 minute read)
item.description: The Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow hacking groups claimed they stole 23TB of data from Russia's state statistics agency, Rosstat. The attackers claim to have stolen data on Russian wartime losses, demographic and economic statistics, and documents marked “for official use only.” Rosstat denied that any databases or legally protected information was leaked.

item.title: Our Latest Defenses Against Evolving Web Scams (5 minute read)
item.description: The Google Chrome team released several new features to further harden the Enhanced Protection mode of Private Browsing. Chrome will now display warnings when a user browses to a suspicious or risky site (depending on confidence level) and provide LLM-based scam detection. Chrome also implemented LLM-based ClickFix attack detection.

item.description: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach security engineers and CISOs where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities.

item.title: Florida Student Aid Website Hack Puts Data of 4.9 Million People at Risk (2 minute read)
item.description: The Florida Department of Education disclosed a breach of its student financial aid website on October 19.

item.title: Germany says lawmakers' iPhones may have been hacked with spyware (2 minute read)
item.description: Germany's BSI has warned that Bundestag members and other prominent figures received Apple's mercenary spyware threat notifications, part of a batch Apple sent to users in 99 countries, and says anyone who gets one should assume their device may have been compromised, although no one has yet been named as behind the attacks.

item.title: Google Introduces $250,000 Root-in-Cloud Bug Bounty Reward (2 minute read)
item.description: Google's Cloud VRP now pays up to $250,000 for exploits that achieve roles/owner or full IAM control over arbitrary Google Cloud tenants, or code execution in its Borg production infrastructure, without existing access, stolen credentials, or user interaction.

item.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours (2 minute read)
item.description: A malicious Claude VS Code extension, version 2.1.313, was published through Anthropic's official Cursor account. It targeted up to 5,000 developers, collected host and environment details, and tried to add an SSH key and open a reverse tunnel. Bugs limited persistence on Windows and macOS. Cursor removed it, blocked its server, rotated keys, and audited the marketplace, but users who installed or updated it on Thursday should check the published indicators of compromise.

item.title: Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script (3 minute read)
item.description: A hijacked DebugBear script on Polymarket's site used signed-in traders' browser sessions to sell or transfer their positions on October 29. Attackers received about $2.64 million in POL from 33 wallets within 52 minutes. Polymarket is refunding $3.9 million, including $2.7 million to 726 affected wallets. The compromise began through DebugBear's domain registrar.

item.title: Binance resumes customer withdrawals after record $6.3bn hack (2 minute read)
item.description: Binance has resumed phased withdrawals after a $6.3 billion theft. The FBI attributes the attack to North Korea-linked TraderTraitor, part of Lazarus Group. The breach involved a compromised laptop and malware that deleted evidence. Binance has replenished 90% of stolen assets and pledged to cover the remainder. The FBI warns that stolen funds are being converted into Ethereum and laundered through DeFi and instant swap services.

item.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer (8 minute read)
item.description: VOLTA takes a "steal everything, let AI sort it out" approach: it grabs credentials, sessions, wallets, and cloud keys, then uses the victim's own Gmail, DoorDash, and Discord sessions to confirm details like a home address. It sends the resulting dossier through OpenRouter to Claude, falling back to Kimi and then Gemini if a model refuses, and gets back a ranked "WHAT THEY'RE WORTH" assessment of what the victim's assets could fetch. Talos assessed VOLTA as a commodity builder that runs entirely on third-party infrastructure. They recommended that defenders block or alert on non-developer processes launching Chrome with --headless, since that is how the stealer gets around App-Bound Encryption.

item.title: Discovering a Backdoor and Flaws in More Encrypted USB Drives (10 minute read)
item.description: Vector 35 researcher Xusheng Li pointed Codex at Binary Ninja's MCP server and recovered the keys hardcoded in NetacFileLock, KakaSoft USB Copy Protection, and Nexcopy Copy Secure in 7 to 26 minutes each. In each product, the key was fixed in the binary, derived from an embedded seed, or unlocked by a certificate in the viewer, so the user's password never protected the files. Separately, time-travel debugging turned up two hidden accounts in SecZure's YutianDun drive, with passwords as weak as "123456", that could decrypt any file. Li skipped vendor disclosure because drives already in the field can't be patched, and he argued that client-side validation is never secure, so buyers should only trust drives that derive their encryption key from the user's password.

item.title: Agentic Offensive Frameworks Hit Real Intrusions (34 minute read)
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant observed intruders using the open-source ARTEX framework with stolen credentials and letting its six sub-agents run Azure and AWS permission sweeps, Kerberoasting, DCSync, and MySQL log poisoning that wrote JSP webshells in bursts as short as 2 to 25 seconds. ARTEX users included financially motivated extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters such as UNC7228, which went from a first account to deep access in about four hours, though GTIG noted the agents were forensically noisy and sometimes undid each other's work. Mandiant recommended short-lived, tightly scoped credentials, locking down admin interfaces like Kudu/SCM as privileged infrastructure, and behavioral detection tuned for machine-speed bursts.

item.title: Northstar Security (Product Launch)
item.description: Northstar Security provides a Security Context Graph from existing security and IT tools. It maps identities, assets, applications, vulnerabilities, and business systems, then flags risky combinations and starts supervised fixes such as installing endpoint protection or limiting access.

item.title: BLA: Blind LLM Agents (GitHub Repo)
item.description: BLA is a tool to harden binaries against agentic reverse engineering. When an AI reverse engineering agent opens the binary, the analyzer his resource budgets, follows decoys, and burns tokens.

item.title: Agentmetry (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Agentmetry is an agent observability tool that records every tool call an agent makes on a machine, flags risky sequences, can block a call that your policy forbids, and keeps a record that a third-party can verify and forward to a SIEM.

item.title: Max-Severity GitLab Vulnerability Exploited Against Alpine Linux (2 minute read)
item.description: CVE-2026-97229, a CVSS 10 flaw in Ruby's Onigmo regex engine, lets unauthenticated attackers execute code through crafted GitLab CI/CD configurations. Attackers targeted Alpine Linux on October 20 to 21, crashed worker processes, and downloaded its container image. Alpine found no confirmed code execution or repository tampering, rebuilt the instance, and reset passwords. CISA added the bug to KEV. GitLab-only updates may be insufficient for custom Ruby deployments. Use Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9, or later.

item.title: Legal Exploits May Emerge At Scale (4 minute read)
item.description: The authors argue that legal systems may have dormant “vulnerabilities” that an attacker can leverage with an LLM to find and exploit. They present an example from the German legal system, which requires executive regulations to cite their legal basis. The authors then showcase a selection of regulations with provisions lacking proper citations, which could render them void and unenforceable.

item.title: CVE-2026-98432: which Linux kernels are still vulnerable (5 minute read)
item.description: Mattias Geniar found 712 Multipath TCP listeners on his own Ubuntu 26.04 laptop, opened without his knowledge by Go programs like tailscaled, because Go 1.24 and later enable MPTCP on listening sockets by default. That matters because the only known exploit for CVE-2026-98432 needs an MPTCP listener. The bug is a use-after-free in the kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake that dates back to Linux 4.4 and can be reached with a single SYN. Upstream stable kernels were fixed in mid-October, and Debian, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK have shipped patches, but Ubuntu and RHEL still had no fixed kernel as of November 1.

item.title: Implant reported in a Trezor sold by CryptoBilis (5 minute read)
item.description: An Indonesian customer reported finding an extra circuit board with a cellular modem inside a Trezor Safe 5 bought from former Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis.

item.title: Belgium's tax agency confirms cyberattack, pulls services offline (2 minute read)
item.description: Belgium's FOD Financiën took MyMinfin, Tax-on-web, and Biztax offline after a cyberattack - there are no indications of a data breach, but investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Applebee's exposed customers' personal data after leaving database password in app (2 minute read)
item.description: A researcher found a hardcoded database password in Applebee's Android app.
